title: The selection inequality as two bars
caption: Top bar: full-data training time. Bottom bar: the selection pipeline's bill -- scorer pass plus training on the subset. Selection is a win only while the bottom bar stays shorter at matched quality; the margin between them is the saving, and scorer cost is what eats it.

title: Coverage floors constrain the score ranking
caption: A score-ranked pool (left) under a three-slot budget and a one-per-slice floor: the rare class keeps its floor slot even with the lowest score, displacing the third-ranked common example. Floors spend opportunity cost on representativeness; a budget smaller than the summed floors is infeasible.

title: The active-learning loop and who pays each stage
caption: Score the unlabeled pool, query the top-k for the oracle, add the new labels, retrain, repeat. The label bill sits at the oracle; the compute bill sits at scoring and retraining -- both enter the inequality against a budget-matched random baseline.

title: Foundation amortization: prepaid versus scratch
caption: From-scratch training costs 1,000 GPU-hours per task; the pretrained path pays 10,000 once and 50 per fine-tune. The lines cross at N = 11 downstream tasks -- below it, self-supervision is the more expensive option; above it, the per-task marginal cost is ~20x lower.

title: The random-access penalty by storage tier
caption: A retained subset scattered across shards turns sequential reads into small random reads. Realized-bandwidth loss for 4 KB reads: ~375x on HDD, ~14x on SATA SSD, under 2x on NVMe. Stream-and-discard keeps sequential speed but still reads every corpus byte; materialized subset shards are what make the saving physical.
